scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: 1. I think you were wrong to visit your son unannounced. While it's understandable that you miss him and want to see him, showing up at his apartment without warning can be seen as an invasion of his privacy and space. Your son is 19 and in university, which means he's trying to establish his independence and set boundaries. By not respecting those boundaries, you may have made him feel uncomfortable and annoyed. It's also important to consider your son's words - he told you that he needs space and that you should give it to him when he needs it. Ignoring his requests for space and showing up unannounced may have reinforced his feelings of being ignored or disrespected, which could damage your relationship with him. Additionally, it's possible that your son is indeed busy with studying and other responsibilities, and your frequent calls may have been adding to his stress. It's essential to find a balance between showing your love and care for your son and respecting his need for independence and space. In the future, it might be better to respect your son's boundaries and communicate with him in a way that works for both of you. You could try asking him when would be a good time to visit or talk, and respect his answer if he says he needs space. This will help you build trust and strengthen your relationship with him.
